## A room, a sound, a date {#cold-open}

***Stanford, late 1982.*** A terminal, a loudspeaker, and two students who have
found that a few dozen memory locations and a single averaging instruction
produce something that sounds unmistakably like a plucked string.[^cold]

This is **beat one, the cold open**: a scene, a sound, a moment. *Italics*
and **bold** are fine here; headings above this level are not. Keep it
around 150 words.

[^cold]: Footnotes are for asides that would interrupt the story. Sources
    go in `sources.bib` instead, and are cited inline like this
    [@karplus1983].

## What couldn't be done {#problem}

Beat two states the problem. Before this milestone, what was impossible,
or too expensive, or too slow? What did musicians do instead?

::: {.column-margin}
A **margin note** sits beside the paragraph. Use it for the FPGA aside, a
date, or a one-line "for the engineers" remark. Keep it under 40 words.
:::

::: {.callout-note .signal icon=false title="Follow the signal"}
**Block A — the signal before.** A signal block answers the one question
the narrative just raised, then stops. Text is visible; code is folded. Here
the question is "what does a simple tone even look like?", so we make one.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ping-waveform
#| fig-cap: "The first 20 ms of a decaying two-partial tone: a fundamental at 440 Hz plus a quieter partial at 1320 Hz."
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "model")
from ping import ping
from sm import FS, io, plot

y = ping()                                   # the model
io.write_wav("out/audio/ping.wav", y)        # keep the artifact on disk
plot.waveform(y, t_max=0.02);
```

The sound itself, rendered by the same code:

```{python}
#| echo: false
from IPython.display import Audio
Audio(y, rate=FS)
```
:::

## The insight {#insight}

Beat three is the idea in plain words, and the audio-critical paragraph. If
a listener hears only this section, they should still come away knowing
*why* the milestone worked. No equations. One image, if any.

> A blockquote for a primary-source line, a quote from the inventor, or an
> advertisement of the period. Attribute it in a footnote or citation.

::: {.callout-note .signal icon=false title="Follow the signal"}
**Block B — the mechanism.** This is the block every essay has. Inline math
is fine here: the fundamental period is $T = 1/f_0$, and the sample delay
that produces it is $N = f_s / f_0$. Display math gets its own line:

$$
y[n] = e^{-\alpha n / f_s}\,\big(\sin(2\pi f_0 n / f_s) + 0.3\,\sin(2\pi\,3 f_0\, n / f_s)\big)
$$

```{python}
#| label: fig-ping-spectrum
#| fig-cap: "Magnitude spectrum of the tone. Two peaks, as promised by the equation."
plot.spectrum(y, f_max=3000);
```

A small table when parameters need listing:

| parameter | value  | meaning                         |
|-----------|--------|---------------------------------|
| $f_0$     | 440 Hz | fundamental                     |
| $\alpha$  | 4 /s   | decay rate                      |
| $f_s$     | 44.1 k | sample rate                     |

: Parameters of the test tone. {.striped}
:::

## The people and the machine {#story}

Beat four is the story proper: who, where, with what constraints, and what
went wrong first. This is usually the longest beat.

::: {.callout-note .signal icon=false title="Follow the signal"}
**Block C — the detail that makes it sound right.** The tweak the inventors
found, or the one everyone gets wrong. Often the most interesting
engineering in the essay. Code here can be shown without executing:

```python
# Shown, not run. Use a plain ```python fence when the point is to read
# the code rather than to produce a figure.
def one_pole_lowpass(x, a=0.5):
    y = np.zeros_like(x)
    for n in range(1, len(x)):
        y[n] = (1 - a) * x[n] + a * y[n - 1]
    return y
```

And an audio file already on disk can be embedded with plain HTML, which
is also exactly how it goes into a Ghost HTML card:

<audio controls src="out/audio/ping.wav"></audio>
:::

## The same model, live {#live}

Everything above was executed here and baked into the page. This block is not:
it loads Python into the reader's browser and runs the essay's own files
against whatever the sliders say.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| label: live-ping-source
# Ship sm/ and this milestone's model to the browser. Read at render time so
# there is one copy of the maths: what the reader drives below is the same
# source that produced the figures above, not a JavaScript restatement of it.
# NOTE: freeze hashes this .qmd, not the files read here — delete this
# milestone's folder in _freeze/ after editing sm/ or model/.
import json
from pathlib import Path

from IPython.display import HTML, display

sources = {f"sm/{p.name}": p.read_text() for p in sorted(Path("../../sm").glob("*.py"))}
sources["model/ping.py"] = Path("model/ping.py").read_text()

# </ inside a <script> would close it early, whatever the JSON says.
blob = json.dumps(sources).replace("</", "<\\/")
display(HTML(f'<script id="live-ping-source" type="application/json">{blob}</script>'))
```

::: {.callout-note .signal icon=false title="Follow the signal, live"}
**Block D — the model in your hands.** `ping()` is a fundamental plus a
quieter partial at three times the frequency, both decaying exponentially.
Reading that is one thing; hearing what the decay rate does to it is another.

```{=html}
<div id="live-ping" class="live-ping">
  <p class="live-ping-status" data-role="status">This block runs Python in your browser.</p>
  <div class="live-ping-controls" data-role="controls" hidden>
    <label>fundamental
      <input type="range" data-role="f0" min="110" max="880" step="1" value="440">
      <output data-role="f0-out">440 Hz</output>
    </label>
    <label>decay
      <input type="range" data-role="decay" min="0.5" max="12" step="0.1" value="4">
      <output data-role="decay-out">4.0 /s</output>
    </label>
  </div>
  <img class="live-ping-plot" data-role="plot"
       alt="Waveform of the tone currently dialled in, first 20 ms.">
  <audio class="live-ping-audio" data-role="audio" controls></audio>
</div>
<script src="../../static/js/live-ping.js" defer></script>
```
:::
